text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Allan Rock regrets harm to Brian Mulroney: Justice Minister concedes he failed to convey his concern for anguish of former PM.
- WHL to use RCMP screening: Police to check for criminal pasts.
- Legal-aid cash squeeze clogs courts: Without counsel, some plead guilty when Crown's case weak, official say.
- Ontario Hydro hires U.S. nuclear experts: Going outside for help with problems at atomic plants a blow to utility's prestige.
- Letter drive linked to Shoppers employee: Owner of Meditrust says he believes campaign scared investors away from mail-order pharmacy.
- Pratt to get Ottawa handout: $147-million loan to Quebec company criticized as favouring companies in that province.
- WIC vote takes bizarre turn: Trustee admits miscount, but outcome remains the same.
- Turmoil hits McCain bottom line: Executive exodus, court loss cut profit of French fry maker.
- Korean-Canadians succeed back home: Some expatriates are returning to their native land and setting up businesses inspired by their education and experiences in Canada.
- Wells Fargo wants to hitch up small business loans.
- Hydro-Quebec's power play: Provincial utility wants to spread its wings in a deregulating energy market. Buying a stake in Noverco, majority owner of Gaz Metropolitain, could further its goal.
